verdicts.flaw_description: "The counts cover the sessions that reached the new page, and a quarter of each segment dropped out before checkout." The purchase counts are restricted to the sessions that got as far as the new checkout page, while a quarter of each segment is dropped before that point; the comparison month is the whole segment. Conditioning the treatment period on progression to checkout selects the more purchase-prone sessions, so the 4-7 percent lift can be pure selection.

"The figures cover the runs with the upgraded filter in service, and a quarter of each stack's runs were made with the filter bypassed." A quarter of the post-upgrade runs - exactly the runs most likely to be high-particulate - are excluded from the treatment-period figures, while the earlier-quarter baseline is the unit's full run history. The 8-14 percent drop is produced by the exclusion rule as much as by the filter.

"Pollen counts in each group's district ran a fifth below the previous quarter, and every group lived and slept on the district's outside air." The report states a confounder that moved in the same direction as the claimed effect and then states that the patients were fully exposed to it rather than shielded from it. A 20 percent fall in pollen exposure would itself reduce attack counts against the prior quarter, so the 4-7 fewer attacks cannot be attributed to the inhaler.

"Averages cover the patients who kept up the home exercises, and a quarter of each intake let the home exercises lapse." The abduction averages are computed only over the adherent patients while a quarter of every intake is discarded, and the earlier-quarter ward baseline is not filtered the same way. Adherence tracks motivation and injury severity, so this adherer-only average inflates the 9-16 degree gain independently of the protocol.

"Rates cover the trays sown from seed that took a full coat, and about a fifth of each lot's trays were sown from partly coated seed." One tray in five is excluded from the germination rate on a criterion (coating quality) that plausibly predicts poor germination, while the previous spring sowing it is compared against had no such exclusion. The 6-11 point gain is measured on a filtered subset.

"Rates cover the boards soldered on the new profile throughout, and about a tenth of each run's boards took one pass on the old profile." The defect rate is computed only on boards that never touched the old profile, dropping roughly a tenth of each run, whereas the earlier-month baseline for the same line includes all boards. Mixed-pass boards are the ones most likely to be defective, so the exclusion alone can produce the 4-7 percent improvement.
